issues.t: Automatic transmission harsh shifts or failure
issues.sym: Harsh or erratic upshifts, a shift lever that is hard to move out of Park, a whine on light acceleration, slipping, or the van no longer pulling in gear.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic shared with the Nissan Quest wears internally. Ford service alerts cover harsh shifts from debris in the valve body, torque converter leaks, transaxle whine and a revised forward clutch, and high-mileage vans eventually fail outright.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition with the engine warm. If it slips or shifts harshly, have it diagnosed soon; catching it early can mean a valve body or fluid repair instead of a full rebuild.

issues.t: Gas pedal sticks or the van lurches from a stop
issues.sym: The accelerator feels stuck at the top of its travel, then gives way suddenly so the van surges or lurches forward, often when pulling away from a stop.
issues.why: Carbon builds up around the throttle plate in the throttle body, so the plate sticks closed until extra pedal force breaks it free. This was the most common owner complaint on these vans, and NHTSA looked at throttle linkage complaints on them.
issues.next: Have the throttle body cleaned and the throttle cable checked. If the pedal sticks while driving, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and pull over.

issues.t: Distributor failure causes stalling or no-start
issues.sym: The engine stalls suddenly, loses power once warmed up, or cranks but won't start.
issues.why: The distributor's shaft bearing can rust and seize, and the cam position sensor built into the distributor can fail as it heats up. Either one cuts the spark.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a shop check for spark while the problem is happening. Replacing the distributor is the usual fix.

issues.t: Hot-weather stalling and long cranking
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts after a short stop on a hot day, stalling in hot weather, or a no-start after the van sits hot.
issues.why: Ford issued service alerts for an improved in-tank fuel pump with a hardened gear and an engine computer update for stalling on these vans.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested while the problem is happening. A newer-design fuel pump and the computer update are the usual fixes.

issues.t: Fuel injector failure causes rough running
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfiring, poor fuel economy or hesitation, sometimes with no check engine light.
issues.why: The fuel injectors on these engines fail or clog with age. Ford also issued a bulletin to update the injector wiring harness when an injector is replaced.
issues.next: Have the injectors tested for balance and leaks. Replace any bad injectors and check the wiring connectors.

issues.t: Check engine light from knock sensor code
issues.sym: A check engine light with a knock sensor code (P0325), sometimes along with rough idle or a light tick.
issues.why: The knock sensor sits under the intake manifold, and its sensor or wiring fails with age. Ford issued service alerts about this code.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed. The engine usually runs fine, but the sensor must work to pass emissions testing; replacement means removing the intake manifold.

issues.t: EGR system faults set a check engine light
issues.sym: A check engine light with EGR flow codes, and sometimes rough idle or pinging.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve and passages clog with carbon, and the valve's control parts fail. Ford issued several EGR diagnosis alerts for these vans.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the EGR valve and passages checked and cleaned before replacing parts.

issues.t: Power door locks lock and unlock on their own
issues.sym: The doors lock or unlock by themselves, cycle repeatedly, or the remote stops working.
issues.why: A door lock actuator or switch shorts out, often from moisture. Ford issued many service alerts about self-activating locks, especially on 1996-1998 vans.
issues.next: Have the faulty door switch or actuator found and replaced. Never leave a child or pet inside, because the van may lock itself.

issues.t: Fuel line connector hoses can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel drips near the fuel tank.
issues.why: Four rubber fuel connector hoses supplied with the fuel tank were made improperly and could crack or split. Ford recalled these vans to inspect and replace the hoses.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 96V-203. Do not drive with a fuel smell; have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Fuel tank vent hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gas smell or fuel dripping, especially after filling the tank full and driving a short distance on a warm day.
issues.why: The fuel tank vent hose can crack, and fuel can push into it and leak when the tank is overfilled and heats up. Ford recalled these vans to replace the hose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-419. Avoid topping off the tank and have any fuel smell checked right away.

issues.t: Battery post can leak acid (recall)
issues.sym: Corrosion around the negative battery post, acid leaking from the battery, or a weak battery.
issues.why: Certain GNB batteries had a defective negative post that could leak acid. In the worst case the battery could fail badly and cause a fire or explosion. Ford recalled these vans to replace the battery.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 97V-184. If the original battery is somehow still in the van, do not jump-start it.

issues.t: Power windows work after the key is off (recall)
issues.sym: The power windows can still be raised for several minutes after the ignition is turned off, as long as the driver door has not been opened.
issues.why: The window system did not meet the federal rule for power windows, which raised the risk of a child being caught. Ford's remedy was a warning label.
issues.next: Never leave children alone in the van. Check your VIN for recall 98V-012.

issues.t: Tail light bulb can fall out of its socket (recall)
issues.sym: A brake light or tail light that stops working, or a bulb that is loose in its socket.
issues.why: Some tail lamp sockets were molded wrong, so the locking tab did not hold the bulb firmly. Ford recalled these vans to replace the sockets.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 99V-347 and walk around the van with the brakes on to check all lights.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle bases may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal use. The buckle could fail to hold in a crash.
issues.why: Some TRW seat belt buckle bases were not properly heat treated and might not meet the federal strength requirement. Ford recalled the affected vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open seat belt recalls at a Ford dealer or on NHTSA's site.

issues.t: Steering gear mounting bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the steering, steering that feels loose or shifts, or no symptoms at all.
issues.why: One or more of the five bolts that hold the steering rack in place may not have been tightened correctly. Ford recalled these vans to check and tighten them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open steering recalls. Have any clunk or looseness in the steering checked before driving further.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle bolt can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat belt buckle that feels loose or wobbles at its base.
issues.why: The plastic trim cover at the base of the front seat belt buckle could get trapped under the anchor bolt and let the bolt loosen over time. Ford recalled about 2,500 early 2001 vans to inspect the buckles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-338. Have any loose belt buckle fixed before carrying a passenger in that seat.

issues.t: Front brakes vibrate and wear quickly
issues.sym: Shaking in the steering wheel or brake pedal when stopping, squealing or grinding, and pads and rotors that wear out fast.
issues.why: These heavy vans are hard on their front brakes, rotors warp from heat, and calipers can stick. Ford issued alerts about brake vibration and noise, and owners report frequent brake jobs.
issues.next: Have the pads, rotors and caliper slides checked. Quality rotors and properly lubricated caliper hardware help the next set last longer.

issues.t: ABS warning light comes on at highway speed
issues.sym: The ABS light comes on while driving, often on the highway, and goes out after the van is restarted.
issues.why: Wheel speed sensor faults and a failing ABS actuator set the light. Ford issued alerts covering ABS codes and actuator replacement on these vans.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but anti-lock braking may be off. Have the ABS codes read to find the bad sensor or part.

issues.t: Rear drum brakes grind, squeal or bind
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing from the rear when braking, especially when cold, or rear brakes that drag and get hot after service.
issues.why: Ford issued alerts for rear drum brake noise and for rear brakes binding or overheating after service on these vans.
issues.next: Have the rear drums, shoes and adjusters inspected and serviced. A dragging brake should be fixed quickly.

issues.t: Brake light switch fault stops the shifter leaving Park
issues.sym: The brake lights stay on with the van parked, the shifter won't come out of Park, or the brake lights don't work.
issues.why: The brake light switch can stick or fail. It also controls the brake-shift interlock, so a bad switch affects both. Ford issued several alerts on this.
issues.next: Have the brake light switch tested and replaced. Check that all brake lights work afterward.

issues.t: Rear A/C lines under the van leak
issues.sym: The A/C, especially in the back, stops cooling, and oily residue shows on the lines running under the van.
issues.why: The long refrigerant lines that run under the body to the rear A/C unit corrode and leak. Ford issued a service alert for leaking rear underbody A/C lines.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested. Replace the leaking line section before recharging the system.

issues.t: A/C blows warm in hot weather
issues.sym: The A/C cools at first but blows warm on very hot days, or stops working again a few months after a repair.
issues.why: Ford issued alerts for low or no A/C performance in high temperatures. Leaks, a weak compressor or cooling fan problems are common causes.
issues.next: Have the refrigerant charge, compressor and condenser fan checked, and find any leak before recharging.

issues.t: Musty smell from the vents
issues.sym: A musty or sour smell from the vents, mostly when the A/C or fan first comes on.
issues.why: Moisture on the A/C evaporator lets mold and bacteria grow. Ford issued a service alert for musty HVAC odor on these vans.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter if fitted and have the evaporator cleaned. Make sure the A/C drain is clear.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from hoses or cylinder head gasket
issues.sym: Coolant puddles, a sweet smell, a low coolant level, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: Coolant hoses harden and leak with age, and Ford issued an alert about aluminum cylinder heads leaking coolant or oil. Many hoses are buried behind the engine, which makes the job hard.
issues.next: Find the leak with a pressure test before it causes overheating. Replace old hoses together if access is hard.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leaks
issues.sym: Oil on the engine, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil spots under the van.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets harden with age and seep oil onto the hot exhaust.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed and the gaskets replaced before oil soaks the spark plug wires or drips onto the exhaust.

issues.t: Radiator fan fails or its connector melts
issues.sym: The engine overheats in traffic or at idle, the fan does not run, or there is smoke or a burning plastic smell from the fan area.
issues.why: The electric radiator fan motor wears out, and its wiring connector can overheat and melt. Owners report fans burning out and, in one case, a fan fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell burning plastic, shut the engine off and check the fan area. Have the fan motor, connector and relay checked before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Broken engine mounts cause clunking
issues.sym: A thump when shifting into gear or accelerating, and more vibration at idle.
issues.why: The engine mounts wear and crack with age and let the engine rock too much.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Replacing a broken mount protects the exhaust, hoses and axles from extra movement.

issues.t: Headlights flicker or the connector melts
issues.sym: Headlights that flicker, go out or dim, and a browned or melted plug behind the bulb.
issues.why: The headlight bulb terminals can create high resistance and overheat the connector housing. NHTSA looked into this, and Ford issued an alert for dim, flickering or dead headlamps.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Replace a melted connector along with the bulb, not just the bulb, or the new one will fail too.

issues.t: Wipers run with the switch off
issues.sym: The windshield wipers keep running or start by themselves with the switch turned off.
issues.why: A fault in the multifunction (wiper and turn signal) switch. Ford issued alerts and a switch replacement procedure.
issues.next: Have the multifunction switch tested and replaced if it is the cause.

issues.t: Sliding door sticks or is hard to close
issues.sym: The sliding door is hard to open or close, sticks partway, or rattles.
issues.why: The door's rollers, tracks and latch wear and get dirty. Ford issued a service alert for sliding doors that are hard to operate.
issues.next: Have the tracks cleaned and lubricated and worn rollers replaced. Make sure the door latches fully before driving.

issues.t: Front stabilizer bar bushings and links wear
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles from the front over bumps, and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Owners report stabilizer bar and bushing failures and rust collecting in the strut mounts on these vans.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked on a lift. Bushings and links are simple to replace.
